<Route path="/ade/dashboard/versions" />

**Versions** is one project's history: every version, its status, its mock, and what changed. Open
it by **clicking a project** on [Projects](./projects.mdx). To move to another project, **click the
project's name** at the end of the breadcrumb: type in **Jump to project** to filter, then **click a
project**. **All projects** at the bottom goes back to Projects. Catalog items are not listed;
convert one to OpenAPI first.

The header holds **“Compare”** (needs two versions), **“Import”**, **More actions** (`⋯`) and
**“New version”**. **More actions** holds:

| Item | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Merge branches…** | Opens the merge dialog. Marked `gitlike`; unavailable until the project has two named branches, and the row says why |
| **Sunset timeline** | Opens the [sunset timeline](/ship) |
| **Published surface** | Opens the published surface |
| **Export studio** | Opens the Export studio, once it is released |
| **Copy link to project** | Copies a link to this project's Versions page (**`⌘ ⇧ C`**) |

The dialogs are on [Version dialogs](./version-dialogs.mdx). Keyboard paths are on
[Keyboard](../workspace/keyboard.md).

## Timeline

<Screenshot id="versions" alt="The Versions page, Timeline tab: the project name as the last breadcrumb, Compare, Import, More actions and New version, the Status strip, the Project facts card, and the version list under its one filter toolbar" caption="Captured from a development build, which also draws git-like controls marked gitlike; production builds hide them." />

From top to bottom:

1. **Status** — one row of chips, one per thing worth knowing: whether the latest change is
   **Compatible** (or has **Breaking changes**), **What’s new** in the draft, and any version that
   is **deprecated**. **Click a chip** to open its detail underneath; only one detail is open at a
   time, and the most urgent one opens on its own. Each detail keeps its actions: **“View
   report”**, **“Open changes”**, **“Sunset timeline”** and **“Migration guide”**. **Click the
   open chip** (or **“Collapse”**, or press <kbd>Esc</kbd>) to hide the detail; the page remembers
   your choice for this project until you close the tab. With nothing to report, the row is not
   drawn.
2. **Project** — id, slug, head version, last publish, and a link to **Published surface**.
3. **The list** — one toolbar on top of the table, then the versions. See [Filter the
   list](#filter-the-list). The columns are **Version**, **Revision / changelog**, **Status**,
   **Mock**, **Created by**, **Created** and actions. Badges mark the **HEAD** version,
   **Published** (read-only) and **Locked** versions.

### Filter the list

Every filter sits in the toolbar on top of the table, left to right:

| Control | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **Search revisions** | Matches the message, changelog, commit body and commit author as you type |
| **All lifecycles** | Shows only **Stable**, **Beta**, **Deprecated** or **Archived** versions |
| **“Any time”** | Opens **Created between**: set **From** and **To**, or **click** **Last 7 days**, **Last 30 days** or **This quarter**, then **click “Apply”**. **“Clear”** removes the range. The button then shows the range, for example **Last 7 days** |
| **“All authors”** | Opens a list of the people who created the versions shown. **Click a name** to see only theirs |
| **All revisions** | Shows the versions reachable from one tag. Shown when the project has tags |
| **All** · **Drafts** · **Published** | Narrows the list by state; each chip shows its count |
| **“Clear filters (n)”** | Appears while any filter is on; **n** is how many. **Click** it to show every version again |
| **Sorted by …** | Sorts by created date, version or another column |

<kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the date box and the author list without changing the filter. The filters are kept in
the page address, so you can **copy the link** to share a filtered list. Switching to another project
clears the search, author, dates, tag and lifecycle; the state chip stays.

### The mock switch

Each row's **Mock** switch serves that version from Apiome's hosted mock. A published version's
mock reads **Mock on** or **Mock off**; a draft's mock is private and needs an API key (**Draft
mock off** until you turn it on). When it is on, the cell shows the mock URL with a copy button,
the **Scenarios** and **Correlation** editors and 30 days of usage. See [One mock
engine](../reference/mock-runtime/one-mock-engine.md).

### Row actions

The row's quick buttons are **Publish** (or **Unpublish**) and **Edit** or **Schedule sunset
(EOL)**. Its **Actions** menu holds:

| Item | Does |
| --- | --- |
| **View spec** | Opens the generated OpenAPI document (JSON or YAML) to copy or download |
| **Export to another format…** | Opens the export dialog — see [Export](./version-dialogs.mdx#export) |
| **Schedule sunset (EOL)…** | Deprecates the version and sets its end-of-life date |
| **Edit** | Changes lifecycle, notes and sunset metadata |
| **Publish** / **Unpublish** | Publishes the version, or takes it back after a confirmation. Unpublishing moves the version's tags back to the previous published version and notifies webhook subscribers — see [Unpublish a version](../ship/publish-a-version.md#unpublish-a-version) |

Git-like actions (branch, fork, tag, freeze, lock, delete) also live here when <Flag
name="FEATURE_GITLIKE"/> is on — it is off in every shipped build. See [Git-like
features](./version-dialogs.mdx#git-like-features). With the flag on, a **Server ahead** chip joins
the status row — on every tab — when someone pushed after you; its detail offers **“Pull”** and
**“Open merge”**.

## Changes

The **Changes** tab lists each published version's classified changelog — breaking, non-breaking
and docs-only changes — which Apiome writes right after a publish.

<Screenshot id="versions-changes" alt="The Changes tab: published versions on the left, the selected version's classified changelog on the right" />

## Test bench

The **Test bench** tab checks a payload against any schema in the project: pick a schema, paste or
generate a payload, and **click “Validate”**. Findings point at the line that failed; saved
payloads become a test suite. It needs a project with a slug.

<Screenshot id="versions-test-bench" alt="The Test bench tab: a schema picker, a payload editor with one finding, generated payloads and saved test payloads" />

## Discussion

The **Discussion** tab collects comment threads on the project's classes, properties, paths and
operations — **Open**, **Resolved**, **Orphaned** or **All**, filtered by kind of element. Its count
is the number of unresolved threads.

<Screenshot id="versions-discussion" alt="The Discussion tab: open comment threads on classes, properties and operations" />

## Repository

The **Repository** tab binds a draft version to a branch of a registered repository. Pick the
**Version**, then under **Bind this draft** choose the **Repository**, a **Branch** and a **Source
path**, and **click “Bind”**. Register repositories first under **Bring in → Repositories**.

<Screenshot id="versions-repository" alt="The Repository tab: an unbound draft, with repository, branch and source path fields" />

## Sources

The **Sources** tab shows which repository files make up the project and where each class and path
of a version came from. This is useful when the API is split across several repositories, one per
service, and each is imported into the same project (see
[Merge several repositories into one project](../bring-in/repositories.mdx#merge-several-repositories-into-one-project)).

1. **Pick the Version.** The newest one is selected first.
2. **Contributing repositories** lists each file in **precedence** order: **1** is the file that was
   imported first. Each row shows how many of the version's classes and paths that file defines, and
   which version it was last imported into.
3. The table lists every class and path of the version, with its **Source** and its **Origin**:

| Origin | Means |
| --- | --- |
| **Imported** | This version's import wrote it from that file |
| **Carried forward** | Another file's import kept it unchanged from the previous version |
| **Not from a repository** | No repository file defined it. It was edited in Apiome, or imported before multi-repository merge |

Use the search box, the **All** / **Classes** / **Paths** chips and the source picker to narrow the
table. Pick **Not from a repository** to see what no file owns.

<Screenshot id="versions-sources" alt="The Sources tab: two contributing repositories in precedence order, and each class and path with its source and origin" />

### Sync back to repositories

Under the contributing repositories, **Sync back to repositories** opens a pull request that writes
the selected version back into each repository's files. Each repository decides in its own
**Settings** tab whether this project may (see
[Send changes back as a pull request](../bring-in/repositories.mdx#send-changes-back-as-a-pull-request)).
A repository that does not allow it shows **Not allowed** and the reason.

1. **Pick the Version** to send back.
2. **Click “Preview”** on a repository. Nothing is written: you see which files would change, how
   many paths and schemas each holds, and the pull request description. Open
   **Pull request description** to read the change report and the commit message.
3. **Click “Open pull request”.** Apiome opens the pull request and shows **View pull request #…**.

<Screenshot id="versions-pr-back-preview" alt="Sync back to repositories: a preview for acme/orders-service with one modified file, and acme/payments-service not allowed" />

What the result means:

| Result | Means |
| --- | --- |
| **Preview** | Nothing was written; this is what a pull request would contain |
| **Pull request opened** | A new pull request was opened |
| **Pull request updated** | The project's open pull request now carries this version |
| **Already up to date** | The open pull request already carries exactly this version |
| **Nothing to sync** | The target branch already holds the rendered files, so nothing was written |
| **Failed** | The pull request could not be opened; the message says why and what to do |

Opening a pull request needs the `versions:publish` permission; **Preview** needs only
`projects:view`.

## Dependencies

The **Dependencies** tab lists what the project depends on and what depends on it — consumers,
declared dependencies, the repository that serves it — with each edge's provenance and owner team,
then draws them. **Click “Blast radius”** to see what a change to one of its operations or schemas
affects. See [Dependency graph](../govern/dependency-graph.mdx#the-dependencies-tab).

## Conversion

When the project was created by [converting a catalog item](../bring-in/convert-to-openapi.md), a
**Conversion** tab shows its conversion history — every projection and the evidence behind it. Other
projects do not have this tab.

## Change report <Flag name="FEATURE_GITLIKE"/>

A **Change report** tab with the publication change report and its templates appears only when
`FEATURE_GITLIKE` is on and `NEXT_PUBLIC_CHANGE_REPORT_UI` is not `0`. `FEATURE_GITLIKE` is a
constant in `apiome-ui/lib/feature-flags.ts` and is `false`, so shipped builds do not show it.

## With the CLI or the API

- CLI: `apiome versions list|get|publish|unpublish|freeze|fork|compatibility|delete`, `apiome mock status|enable|disable` — see
  the [`versions` command reference](../reference/cli/versions.md) and the [CLI
  quick-start](../reference/cli-quickstart.md). To take a release back with a recorded reason, see
  [Unpublish a version](../ship/publish-a-version.md#unpublish-a-version). To pin the published
  OpenAPI document byte-for-byte, see [Freeze a version's schema](../ship/publish-a-version.md#freeze-a-versions-schema).
  To fail a build when a new version breaks the previous one, see the
  [version compatibility gate](../reference/ci/version-compatibility-gate.md).
- REST: `GET` / `POST /v1/versions/{tenant}/{project}`, `PUT /v1/versions/{tenant}/{project}/{version}`,
  `…/publish`, `…/unpublish`, `PUT …/mock`, `POST /v1/versions/{tenant}/{project}/fork`,
  `GET /v1/versions/{tenant}/sunset-timeline` — see the [API reference](../reference/api-reference.md).
  The **Sources** tab reads `GET /v1/tenants/{tenant}/projects/{project}/repository-sources?version=…`
  — see [Project repository sources](../reference/rest/project-repository-sources.md). **Sync back to
  repositories** calls `POST /v1/tenants/{tenant}/projects/{project}/pr-back` — see
  [PR-back](../reference/rest/pr-back.md).

### Fork a version into another project from the CLI

A **fork** copies one version of a project into **another** project as a new draft version, and
records where it came from so it can be merged back later. (To start a new version inside the same
project, branch it instead.) The CLI can fork whether or not the Git-like features are switched on
in the web app.

1. **Preview** what would be copied:
   `apiome versions fork payments-api v2.1.0 --into payments-sandbox --to 3.0.0 --dry-run`.
   The source can be a version label (`2.1.0` or `v2.1.0`), a revision id, or a version tag.
2. **Fork** it by running the same command without `--dry-run`. Add `--notes '…'` for a short note,
   `--notes-file CHANGELOG.md` for release notes, and `--include-tags` to recreate the tags that
   point at the source version.
3. The fork copies the version's **classes and their properties**. **Paths are not copied** — the
   summary says how many the source has.

`--to` must be a plain release version (`3.0.0`, not `3.0.0-rc.1`) and greater than the source's
— pass `--allow-lesser` to go lower. If the target project already has that version, nothing is
forked and the command exits `6`. With `--json` it prints the new version.

### List version tags from the CLI

Version tags (`stable`, `latest`, `prod` …) are named pointers to a version.
`apiome tags list <project>` shows each tag, the version it points to, its channel, when it was
last updated and who created it; `apiome tags show <project> <tag>` shows one tag in full, including
whether it is immutable or protected.

```bash
apiome tags list payments-api
# TAG     POINTS TO  CHANNEL  UPDATED     CREATED BY
# latest  2.1.0               2026-05-04  kenji@example.com
# prod    2.0.0               2026-02-18  kenji@example.com
# stable  2.1.0      stable   2026-05-04  kenji@example.com

apiome tags show payments-api stable
```

`tags list` shows the first 50 tags; pass `--limit N` or `--all`. Both commands take `--json`.
Apiome keeps only a tag's current pointer — it records who created a tag, not who moved it — so
there is no move history to show.

### Create a version tag from the CLI

`apiome tags create <project> <tag> --version <version>` points a new tag at a version.

```bash
apiome tags create payments-api stable --version v2.1.0
# ✔ Tag 'stable' created → 2.1.0.

apiome tags create payments-api prod-eu --version v2.0.0 \
  --description 'Production EU release pinned for compliance review'
```

- Tag names are **lower-cased** and must be 2–41 characters: a letter, then letters, digits or
  hyphens (`stable`, `prod-eu`). Names such as `latest`, `stable` and `next` are conventions, not
  reserved.
- If the project already has a tag with that name, nothing is created and the command exits `6` —
  move the existing tag instead.
- `--from-file tag.json` reads a JSON tag object (an edited `apiome --json tags show` works);
  flags on the command line win over the file. A file can also set `channel` and `immutable`. An
  **immutable** tag can never be moved or deleted, so the command asks first — pass `--yes` to skip.
- With `--json` it prints the created tag.

### Move a version tag from the CLI

`apiome tags update <project> <tag> --version <version>` moves a tag — the usual "promote 2.1.0 to
stable".

```bash
apiome tags update payments-api stable --version v2.1.0
# Moving 'stable' from 2.0.0 → 2.1.0.
# Affected consumers of 2.0.0 (best effort):
#   Mock requests, last 7 days: 23
#   Frozen-snapshot downloads:  4
#   Other tags on 2.0.0:        prod
# Continue? [y/N]: y
# ✔ Tag 'stable' now points to 2.1.0.
```

1. **Run** the command. It shows where the tag points now and, as a guide to who may be affected,
   what Apiome knows about that version: mock requests in the last 7 days, downloads of its frozen
   snapshot, and the other tags on it. Apiome does not count spec downloads per version, and a figure
   it cannot read shows as *unavailable* — it never stops the move.
2. **Answer `y`** to move it, or pass `--yes` in a script. `--dry-run` shows the same summary and
   changes nothing.

`--description '…'` sets the tag's description at the same time (`--description ''` clears it); with
`--version` set to where the tag already points, only the description changes. An **immutable** tag
can never be moved — the command exits `6`. With `--json` it prints the updated tag.

### Delete a version tag from the CLI

`apiome tags delete <project> <tag>` removes a tag you no longer use — an old release-candidate
channel, say. Only the tag goes: the version it points to is not touched.

```bash
apiome tags delete payments-api next-rc
# Deleting tag 'next-rc' (currently points to 2.2.0). The version itself is not touched.
# Type the tag name to confirm: next-rc
# ✔ Deleted tag 'next-rc'.
```

1. **Run** the command with the tag's name (or its id).
2. **Type the tag name** exactly as shown to confirm, or pass `--yes` in a script.

An **immutable** tag can never be deleted — the command exits `6`. A protected tag needs a tenant
administrator. With `--json` it prints `{ "deleted": true, "tag": "next-rc", "was_pointing_to": "2.2.0" }`.

### Delete a version from the CLI

`apiome versions delete <project> <version>` removes a version you no longer need — a typo in the
version number, an abandoned spike. It is meant for **drafts**.

1. **Run** `apiome versions delete payments-api v2.2.0`. The command shows the version, its state
   and how many classes and paths it has.
2. **Type the version** exactly as shown to confirm (or pass `--yes` in a script).

```bash
apiome versions delete payments-api v2.2.0
# This will delete:
#   • Version:  2.2.0  (state: draft)
#   • Classes:  24
#   • Paths:    18
# No published artifacts will be affected.
# The version disappears from every list and spec URL; only a database administrator can restore it.
# Type the version to confirm (2.2.0): 2.2.0
# ✔ Deleted 2.2.0.
```

- **Version tags** pointing at the version stop the delete — the command lists them. Pass
  `--detach-tags` to remove them first.
- A **published** or **frozen** version is refused (exit `6`). `--force` takes it through the safe
  paths first: it is [unpublished](../ship/publish-a-version.md#unpublish-a-version) with
  `--reason` (webhook subscribers are notified, tags move back to the previous published version),
  its [frozen snapshot](../ship/publish-a-version.md#freeze-a-versions-schema) is removed (a
  downloaded snapshot needs a tenant administrator), and any remaining tags are removed.
- With `--json` it prints `{ "deleted": true, "version": "2.2.0", "removed_tags": [...], ... }`.
